questions.html:
Consider the following language $\mathrm{L}$ with the alphabet $\{0,1\}$. The empty string is not in $\mathrm{L}.$ If the string is nonempty and has even length, then it is in $\mathrm{L}.$ If the string has odd length, then it is in $\mathrm{L}$ if and only if it is a palindrome.

Which of the following best describes $\mathrm{L}?$
questions.solution:
Answer: C

questions.html:
A grammar is said to be "useless" if and only if it produces no terminal strings. If $\text{S}$ is the start symbol, which of the following grammars is (are) "useless"?

  1. $\begin{aligned}&\text{S} \rightarrow \text{AB} \mid \text{AS}\\ &\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B} \mid a\\ &\text{B} \rightarrow \text{A} \mid b \end{aligned}$

 

  1. $\begin{aligned} &\text{S} \rightarrow \text{SA}\mid \text{AS}\mid \text{SB}\\ &\text{A} \rightarrow a\\ &\text{B} \rightarrow a \mid b \end{aligned}$

 

  1. $\begin{aligned} &\text{S} \rightarrow \epsilon \mid \text{A} \\ &\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B} \\&\text{B} \rightarrow \text{C} \\&\text{C} \rightarrow a \end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
Answer: B

questions.html:
A context-free grammar has a set of terminals $\{0,1,-\}$, a set of non-terminals $\{\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{P}\}$, where $\mathrm{N}$ is the start symbol, and productions given by the following .
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{N} \rightarrow 0 \mid \mathrm{P} \mid -\;\mathrm{P} \\
&\mathrm{P} \rightarrow 1 \mid \mathrm{P}\; 0 \mid \mathrm{P} \;1
\end{aligned}
$$
What can be said about the language generated by this grammar?
questions.solution:
Answer: A

  • There are never more than three consecutive rainy days, and
  • There are never more than five consecutive non-sunny days.

The language of $\text{GO}$-like sequences is
questions.solution:
Answer: A
